title: Structured output field duplication and attribution mismatch after multi-region failover with dedupe layer enabled
creator: Avery Chen
description: Multiple customers reported production failures where a tool/function call returned duplicate fields in the structured JSON payload or fields were attributed to the wrong invocation after traffic was failed over between regions or when proxy replay occurred. Affected flows span Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments when the optional response deduplication/merge layer is enabled in the request pipeline. Symptoms: duplicated keys, shifted value pointers (e.g., tool_response.body appears in tool_response_alt), and downstream parsers raising StructuredParseError causing customer incidents.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use a multi-region tenant with dedupe_layer=true and request routing policy set to fallback-to-region-b when region-a capacity is constrained.
2) Trigger a user request that includes a function/tool call which returns a nested JSON body and large streaming chunks.
3) Force an edge failover or simulate a proxy replay (close and reconnect edge connection during streaming).
4) Observe reassembled response at the backend: duplicate fields, mismatched invocation_id mapping, or malformed nested JSON that previously parsed successfully.
investigation_notes: Initial customer report came from an enterprise customer running on Dedicated (customer ticket #INC-2026-134).

Reproduced in lab by replaying a buffered streaming response while toggling the dedupe layer — failure only appears when the dedupe/merge component receives overlapping segments with non-monotonic sequence markers.

Logs show two distinct events with same client_invocation_id arriving from different edge proxies after failover; dedupe layer merged them by key rather than by sequence, producing duplicate keys or misattributed sub-objects.
KV cache metadata (session_tag) was present but sometimes not forwarded by older private proxies, increasing collision probability.
Parser stacktrace indicates StructuredParseError at the step that maps tool call envelopes into invocation records (runtime/parse/envelope_mapper.go:214).
Root cause appears to be a combination of: non-unique per-segment sequence tokens across proxies + dedupe merge strategy that uses shallow key equality instead of stable invocation fingerprint.
root_cause: Dedupe/merge layer incorrectly merges overlapping response segments using shallow JSON-key matching when sequence tokens are non-monotonic across proxied replay/failover, causing duplication and misattribution of tool output fields. Private/Dedicated proxies that drop or rewrite session tags increase collision likelihood.
proposed_fix: 1) Make dedupe layer merge deterministic by using a stable invocation fingerprint: concat(client_invocation_id, region_id, monotonic_segment_index) and prefer higher monotonic_segment_index. 2) Harden proxies to preserve session_tag and monotonic segment index; add validation and reject segments missing required headers. 3) Add defensive reparsing that detects duplicate keys in tool envelopes and flags them for safe fallback to the original raw stream. 4) Add integration tests and chaos tests that simulate edge failover + proxy replay.
rollout_plan: Phase A (hotfix to lab): update dedupe layer to prefer explicit sequence index and enable aggressive validation (canary on staging). Phase B (beta): deploy to a small set of Dedicated customers and internal load tests. Phase C (gradual rollout): staged rollout to Hosted with feature flag off by default for tenants with non-compliant proxies. Phase D: for Private customers, provide a patch and a proxy upgrade bundle; coordinate with SEs for scheduled windows.
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests covering: single-stream with replay, multi-stream interleaving, and non-monotonic segment sequences.
Reproduction steps from customers no longer produce duplicate keys in the lab environment.
Observed reduction to zero of StructuredParseError related to tool-call duplication for canary tenants over 72h.
Proxy validation rejects malformed/missing session_tag headers and logs a telemetry event for ops to monitor.
stakeholders: Design: Jonah Patel (for UX error messages)
followups: Audit dedicated/private proxy versions and produce a compatibility matrix — assign ENG-553211.
Add telemetry metric for dedupe-merge collisions and create an alert — assign ENG-553212.
Customer communications: draft incident summary and notify affected customers with mitigation steps — ownership Support/Customer Success.
Schedule a retro with Engineering, Network, and Support to capture operational gaps.
